task.outcome:
Prevent palace writers from reusing another thread's installation lease. Reproduced at current source 97d4a7b52d39d64e00698035603c9bc1e4ee9fa3; owners unchanged from 7c8a506a. Exclusive maintenance in thread A blocks thread B's direct shared acquisition, but thread B enters palace_write_lease. A second regression shows a writer reuses another thread's shared lease and no longer blocks maintenance after the other thread releases. Existing tests/test_uat_leases.py and operation_lock.py module contract independently require maintenance exclusion, same-thread nesting and per-palace serialization. Before evidence: .codex-local/greptile-repeat-20261002/before.log (two failed regressions). Rule Zero: extend current in-process hold registry with acquisition-thread ownership; preserve process-level introspection and explicit migration inheritance. Applicable LDR selection is explicitly empty: docs/decisions absent and no accepted record bound to these owners; this restores current contracts without a new architectural owner.
